scenes.text: How a playing-card maker from Kyoto became one of the biggest names in games.
In 1889, Fusajiro Yamauchi founded Nintendo Koppai in Kyoto to make hanafuda playing cards.
In July 1983 came the Family Computer. Two years later it reached America as the NES.
In 1989 the Game Boy arrived. With the Game Boy Color, it sold over one hundred and eighteen million units.
In 2006, the Wii and its motion controls brought a whole new audience to video games.
And in 2017, the Switch turned a home console into one you can carry.

milestones.headline: Nintendo Koppai
milestones.detail: Fusajiro Yamauchi opens a shop in Kyoto making hanafuda playing cards.

milestones.headline: Family Computer
milestones.detail: The Famicom goes on sale in Japan, and reaches North America as the NES in 1985.

milestones.headline: Game Boy
milestones.detail: A handheld with swappable cartridges, later joined by the Game Boy Color.

stat.label: Game Boy + Game Boy Color units sold

milestones.headline: Wii
milestones.detail: Motion controls bring families and first-time players to video games.

milestones.headline: Nintendo Switch
milestones.detail: A hybrid console that plays on the TV and in your hands.
